Top candidates: **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (ring spots, bronzing, necrotic spots), Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus (mosaic pattern), Early_Blight (concentric rings but darker), Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.

Let me view reference images one by one starting with my top candidate.

This is an almost perfect match to the test image — identical ring spot patterns, same mottled green appearance, same dark necrotic spots, even from the same Bugwood source (5606270 vs 5606275). Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus is very strongly confirmed. Now I need to view 7 more classes to fulfill the budget requirement.
CMV shows distorted, stunted shoestring leaves — very different from the test image. Moving on.
Early Blight shows dark, concentrated lesions — not the diffuse ring pattern seen in the test image.
Septoria shows small discrete spots with dark borders — not the ring/mosaic pattern in the test image.

All 8 views complete. The comparison is clear:

- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (Bugwood_11): Near-identical match — same ring/circular patterns across the whole leaf, same mottled green appearance, same scattered dark necrotic spots, even from the same Bugwood photo series (5606270 vs 5606275).
- All other classes (CMV, Early Blight, Septoria, Late Blight, Powdery Mildew, Verticillium Wilt, Leaf Mold) showed clearly different symptoms.
